headline.why: The human-vs-agent divergence is the finding and needs the baseline in the title. Option a says 'never cheat', yet agents report partners; 'never break' in b is also ambiguous.
headline.better_wording: LLM pricing agents keep cartels humans break, yet told leniency and rewards deter them far more

novelty.why: Replays a 2012 human design cell by cell, but measuring leniency and rewards on LLM agents against a human baseline is new; the instruments were named, never measured.

execution_evidence.why: Shared wording across three regimes is a good within-design argument, but no placebo (prohibition words, zero penalty) exists, fine_certain is pending, and reasons are unanalysed, so the mechanism story stays interpretation.

figure1_30s.why: Eight panels, code-style axis labels, two captions; the reproduction rule concerns regime differences, which no panel shows; panels 7 and 8 plot LLM points while labelled not tested.
figure1_30s.fix: Plot per result the regime difference with interval against the human direction; grey out untested panels without data; plain axis labels; drop the embedded title.

cuts_to_8_pages.cheapest_cut: Drop the pilot row from Table 1; the text already states the positive-control pass.
cuts_to_8_pages.better_cut: Keep a compact n-table; cut the reading guide, the HKCC paragraph and the Conclusion that repeats the abstract.
cuts_to_8_pages.why: Denominators, invalid answers and convictions are exactly what an assurance reviewer checks first; repeated prose and rubric signposting carry no evidence and cost nothing to remove.

must_fix_before_submission: Fill every [F??]; report known-effect arms and shifted grid even if unfavourable.
Use one measure consistently: abstract mixes incidence and formation rates for leniency and reward.
Leniency convictions: text says 9 with 7 reports, Table 3 lists 3 detection plus 7 report.
Reconcile seeds: Methods uses seeds 1 to 4 per regime, Appendix C one seed per regime.
Reconcile pilot '3 duopolies' with '6 of 6 late duopolies' and the stated per-regime cost range.
biggest_risk: Headline results rest on one model, 4 clusters and 10 and 4 cartels; with known-effect arms, placebo and shifted grid still empty, execution reads as preliminary rather than validated.
three_questions: Does a placebo regime with the prohibition wording but zero penalty reduce cartel formation as much as the fine regime?
With 4 pool sessions and only 10 and 4 cartels under leniency and reward, does the result hold on a second model or provider?
Is the exact 0.716 laissez-faire formation match a coincidence, and how sensitive is it to temperature, firm names and prompt paraphrase?
